vertices.label: Concept

frequency_analysis.description: The top 8 components cover approximately 75% of practical competence for most agent development tasks
frequency_analysis.analysis_notes:
Learner can achieve 50% competence with 4 core components (agent loop, custom tools, hooks, subagents). Additional 8 components (total 12) gets to 80%. Remaining 18 components are specialization. Gateway nodes create natural learning progression: master foundations first, then expand tool capabilities, then scale with subagents.

Re-research pass (2026-03-12): Discovered programmatic tool calling (37% token reduction via code_execution tool, GA Feb 2026) and secure deployment patterns (defense-in-depth Docker/gVisor/Firecracker hardening). Added tool search for 85% reduction in tool-definition tokens, memory tool for cross-session persistence, and long-running agent patterns including initializer+worker split and progress.txt documentation.

failure_points.description: Treating SDK like LangChain — trying to build explicit chains/graphs instead of letting the agent loop handle orchestration naturally
failure_points.mitigation: Explicit contrast exercises: build same task with LangChain-style graph vs SDK agentic loop; highlight differences. Early reading of 'Agent Loop & Query Mechanics' required.

failure_points.description: Over-permissive permissions — using bypassPermissions or 'allow' mode in production, creating security risks
failure_points.mitigation: Start with restrictive permissions (default 'prevent'), deliberately loosen only when needed. Practice permission design with safe-mode sandbox exercises.

failure_points.description: Context window management wall — agents work on small tasks but fail on complex ones due to context exhaustion; learner doesn't understand compaction strategies
failure_points.mitigation: Deliberate compaction strategy exercises; early exposure to prompt caching. Build simple agent with logging to show context growth.

failure_points.description: Multi-agent complexity explosion — adding more subagents makes things worse, not better; learner doesn't know when orchestration is harmful
failure_points.mitigation: Start with single-agent, add agents only when single-agent approach fails. Teach: 'One agent per focused responsibility.' Monitor inter-agent communication overhead.

failure_points.description: From 'make it work' to 'make it observable' — early agents work but are black boxes; learner struggles to debug or improve in production
failure_points.mitigation: Build tracing in from day 1, not after-the-fact. Integrate Langfuse or Arize in Week 1 simple agent. Show how observability makes debugging 10x easier.

failure_points.description: System prompt engineering — prompts that work in simple cases fail in complex multi-turn agent interactions; learner overestimates generalization
failure_points.mitigation: Test prompts with adversarial/edge-case scenarios early. Create adversarial prompt examples that fail. Teach prompt iteration with real feedback.

failure_points.description: Assuming LangChain patterns transfer directly — some do, some cause subtle bugs; learner doesn't realize incompatibility until production
failure_points.mitigation: Explicit 'what's different' mapping exercises. Create side-by-side code examples showing patterns that work vs don't work.

failure_points.description: Tool design complexity — building tools that agents misuse or call incorrectly; learner doesn't understand tool semantics
failure_points.mitigation: Teach tool design heuristics: 'Verb-noun naming, atomic operations, clear errors, idempotent where possible.' Include tool design testing in early weeks.

failure_points.description: Cost explosion in multi-agent systems — learner creates runaway agent cascades with hidden cost feedback loops
failure_points.mitigation: Set max_budget_usd aggressively (e.g., $1) in development. Require per-subagent cost budgets. Weekly cost reviews mandatory in early projects.
